Dear Honorable Colleagues,

I respectfully submit this report on the work of the Preliminary Screening Committee for the Council Budget/Management Analyst position.

The Committee received over 40 applications, selected 11 individuals for interviews and, after some withdrawals, interviewed 8 applicants in executive session. We recommend for your consideration the following four individuals, in no particular order: Susan Carmel, Gary Frisch, Frederique Pierre-Lyne Phanor, and Katherine Foster. Their resumes are attached.

The Committee met seven times, September 14, 16, 24, and 28 and October 5, 6, and 14. At our first public meeting, we received a briefing and useful handouts from Mr. Perry, a copy of which is included herewith. Also included is a copy of the posted job description and written guidance from the solicitor's office about the screening process. To assist the full Council when preparing to interview the selected finalists, I am also providing herein some questions you may wish to consider when developing your own.

Along with my colleagues on the Committee, Councilors Spang and Rotondo, we hope the materials included with this filing will not simply be useful now, but also will create some institutional memory for the Council in the future. Two pieces of advice from Mr. Perry are worth noting here: first, the Council (probably through the Finance & Property Subcommittee) should have evaluated him and his work on some regular basis over the years and recommends we adopt this as a policy. Also, he suggests the Council consider and be open to how this position could function differently in the future, as he notes he essentially defined for himself the scope of the position, as he had no transitional hand-off from his predecessor.

In closing, the Committee wishes to thank Mr. Perry for his initial briefing in this process and his many years of exemplary service to the Council and the city.

Respectfully,

Scott Houseman
City Councilor, Ward 4

No, a municipal employee cannot get paid by two different communities for the exact same working hours. Doing so is a direct violation of Massachusetts state ethics laws and is legally considered a form of fraud known as "double dipping."

The explicit rules regarding this practice dictate that:

## 1. Theft & Public Funds

If you are clocked in or collecting an hourly wage from Municipality A, you are legally required to be performing services for Municipality A. If you are simultaneously collecting hourly pay from Municipality B during those same exact hours, you are misrepresenting your time to at least one (if not both) of your employers. This can trigger an investigation by the Massachusetts Office of the Inspector General for fraud, waste, and abuse of public funds. [1]

## 2. Violating the Conflict of Interest Law (G.L. c. 268A, § 23)

Under Section 23 of the Massachusetts Conflict of Interest Law, public employees are strictly prohibited from using their official positions to secure "unwarranted privileges" of substantial value. Getting paid twice for a single hour of work is explicitly classified as an unwarranted privilege and can result in severe financial penalties from the State Ethics Commission. [1]

## The Only Permissible Overlaps

You can only receive money from two different municipalities during the same calendar day if:

- **Distinct Shifts:** You work a defined shift for Town A (e.g., 7 AM to 3 PM) and a separate, non-overlapping shift for Town B (e.g., 4 PM to 8 PM).
- **Approved Paid Time Off (PTO):** You are physically working for Town B while on an approved, pre-planned vacation day or personal day from Town A. (Note: You cannot do this while on paid sick leave from your primary job, as that implies you are too ill to work).
- **Stipend or Elected Roles:** One of the positions pays a flat annual stipend for an elected role or a board seat that does not tie pay directly to specific operational hours, though extreme caution and an official disclosure must still be filed to ensure no duties conflict.

# GUIDANCE TO PUBLIC BODIES RESPONSIBLE FOR HIRING AN EMPLOYEE

(Prepared by Solicitor's Office and Review by KP Law January 2020))

The purpose of this guidance is to advise on compliance with the Open Meeting Law when a public body is responsible for hiring an employee. This memo does not cover HR functions such as creating a job description, advertising, collection of resumes, etc.

## A. *A Public Body may Establish a Subcommittee for the "Preliminary Screening" of Applicants, which Committee is Subject to All of the Requirements of the Open Meeting Law*

A "Preliminary screening" is defined as: "the initial stage of screening applicants conducted by a committee or subcommittee of a public body solely for the purpose of providing to the public body a list of those applicants qualified for further consideration or interview." MGL ch. 30A, section 18. **The Preliminary Screening Committee must be comprised of less than a quorum of the appointing authority.**

The Preliminary Screening Committee must post in accordance with the Open Meeting Law notice of all meetings, or of meetings when two or more members are authorized by the Committee to act collectively. The notice must list, with specificity, the matters to be addressed by the Committee, such that a person reading the notice who is unfamiliar with the issue can reasonably anticipate the subject matter of the discussion.

There is a presumption under the Open Meeting Law that all meetings will be held in open session, unless an executive session is noticed and held in accordance with the Open Meeting Law. For that reason, a Preliminary Screening Committee may meet in executive session only, "To consider or interview applicants for employment or appointment by a preliminary screening committee if the chair declares that an open meeting will have a detrimental effect in obtaining qualified applicants." Although this process may include review of resumes and then one or more rounds of interviews, **this exception does not apply once applicants have passed the preliminary screening**. MGL ch. 30A, section 21(a)(8). **Therefore, once the screening committee has identified finalists to present to the appointing authority, it can no longer meet in executive session to discuss the same.**

Detailed minutes must be taken in executive session. While a transcript of the meeting need not be made, the minutes must provide, with specificity, an outline of the conversations had and the actions taken, including questions asked and answers given. Such minutes must be approved timely (three weeks or three meetings, whichever is later), and then preserved as permanent records. Be aware that candidates at the beginning of a hiring process typically have a higher degree of privacy than those identified as finalists. For that reason, consultation should be had with the City Solicitor's office prior to responding to a public records request for the same.

## B. *Detailed Steps for Proceeding with a Preliminary Screening/Hiring Committee if the Public Body So Chooses*

1) The Public Body establishes Preliminary Screening/Hiring subcommittee, **which must include fewer than a quorum of the Public Body's membership**, and may include persons not part of the Public Body.

2) Subcommittee posts initial meeting. Such posting must occur 48 hours before any meeting (not including Saturdays, Sundays or holidays), listing with specificity the matters to be discussed. Similar notice of all subsequent meetings must be posted as well.

3) The notice for the first meeting should include, but not be limited to the following:

   a. Organization \u2013 elect Chair, Vice Chair and Clerk

   b. Establish overall process \u2013 including, at a minimum the number of candidates to be recommended to the appointing authority as finalists (typically no less than three)

   c. Consider establishing protocols for maintaining privacy of applicants and or applicant materials

   d. Consider establishing uniform questions to be asked of applicants

4) Minutes of all discussions in open and executive session must be taken and approved timely. To enter executive session, the Public Body must take a roll call vote after specifically identifying the purpose for the executive session (which purpose must also be included in the meeting notice); all votes in executive session must also be taken by roll call vote.

5) Resumes for applicants may be distributed to the subcommittee outside of a meeting, but no deliberation may occur. To avoid potential violations of the Open Meeting Law, no member of the Preliminary Screening Committee should "reply to all" on any e-mails forwarding such information. Remember, as well, that candidates, particularly at the beginning of a hiring process, have a significant privacy interest in the fact of their candidacy. For that reason, any such materials must be maintained in a confidential manner.

6) Once resumes are available (at first meeting, or at a future meeting), when the Preliminary Screening Committee wishes to discuss the resumes, the Committee ~~should/may~~ enter into executive session. All meetings, however, must start in an open session and a roll call vote must be made in order to go into executive session. The Chair should announce whether or not the group will reconvene in open session.

7) If the Preliminary Screening Committee anticipates going into executive session, an item for such purposes must be included on any meeting notice. The purpose of the executive session must be stated in each case. For a Preliminary Screening Committee, the notice would say something similar to the following: **To consider or interview applicants for employment or appointment by a preliminary screening committee if the chair declares that an open meeting will have a detrimental effect in obtaining qualified applicants in accord with M.G.L. ch. 30A, section 21(a)(8), and particularly, for [reviewing initial resumes] [conducting interviews] [identifying finalists] [or something similar].**

8) During executive session, the Preliminary Screening Committee may discuss particular candidates and identify individuals to call in to interview.

9) The Preliminary Screening Committee should, either at the end of the executive session if the Chair indicates that the Committee will reconvene, or at the next meeting, report in open session in open session that it has identified candidates for interviews, and has set a meeting date for the interviews (if such date has been selected at that time).

10) A meeting notice should be posted indicating that there will be an executive session to consider and interview applicants, such as the following: **To consider or interview applicants for employment or appointment by a preliminary screening committee if the chair declares that an open meeting will have a detrimental effect in obtaining qualified applicants in accord with M.G.L. ch. 30A, section 21(a)(8), and particularly, for conducting interviews.** Again, to the extent that the only action to be taken by the Public Body at a meeting is to meet in executive session, the words "Open Session" or "Convene the Meeting in Open Session" should appear as the first "item" on the meeting notice.

11) The **interviews of candidates not identified as finalists should be conducted in executive session to protect the privacy interests of such candidates**. Detailed minutes of the interviews should be taken, including questions asked, by who, and answers provided. Such minutes must be approved within the three next meetings, or three weeks, whichever occurs later. Any votes taken in executive session must be taken by roll call vote (recording that a vote was "unanimous" does not meet the requirement for a "roll call" vote.

12) Following the interviews, whether at the same meeting or at a meeting called for the particular purpose, the Preliminary Screening Committee may continue to discuss the applicants in executive session.

13) Ultimately the Preliminary Screening Committee must identify a list of finalists to present to the Public Body for its consideration. Typically, as a courtesy before the names of persons identified as finalists are released, the finalists are notified of this fact and given the opportunity to withdraw. If a person withdraws, and the Committee has identified a particular number of finalists that it will recommend, it may meet in executive session to identify another finalist or finalists. Once the Committee identifies ~~the finalists, it can no longer meet in executive session to discuss the same. Note: Two or~~ **more finalists must be presented to the Public Body for its consideration in order to ensure compliance with the Open Meeting Law.**

## C. *Consideration by Quorum of Public Body After Review by Screening Committee*

1) The Public Body must post a meeting at which it will consider the finalists. The meeting notice should list the names of the finalists to be interviewed, as well as identify the position for which they are being considered. The interviews and any discussion of the finalists may only be held in open session. If resumes of the finalists are made available, they should be redacted to withhold private information such as home address, home telephone number and private e-mail address.

2) To ensure that the Public Body, and the public, understand the process used by the Preliminary Screening Committee, it is often useful to include an item on the meeting notice specifically for such purposes.

3) The Public Body may interview candidates, and or discuss the candidates, at one or more open meetings. There is no limit on the number of times a candidate may be interviewed in open session.

4) Particularly when the decision making is spread over more than one meeting, the meeting at which a decision to appoint or hire will be made should include the words "Votes may be taken", to ensure that the public understands that a vote may occur.

## D. *If a Public Body Chooses to Not Form a Screening Committee*

If a screening committee is **not** used, a public body may **not** go into executive session in reliance on M.G.L. ch. 30A, section 21(a)(8) "to consider or interview applicants for employment or appointment".

Exemption (7), however, allows a body to meet in executive session to comply with "the provisions of any general or special law or federal grant-in-aid requirements." Massachusetts General Laws ch. 214, section 1B, provides a right against "an unreasonable, substantial or serious interference with" personal privacy. Thus, a Public Body may meet in executive session pursuant to exemption (7) to consider the resumes of all applicants and decide who it may want to interview. Such persons are known as "semi-finalists", and must be interviewed in open session. As indicated above, there is no limit to the number of times a person may be interviewed in open session.

To ensure that a Public Body properly invokes this exemption, each and every applicant should confirm that they would not be willing to participate in the process if their name was disclosed prior to being named as a semi-finalist.

# JOB DESCRIPTION

**Title:** City Council Budget/Management Analyst

**Reports To:** Beverly City Council President and Beverly City Council

**Appointment:** Elected by the City Council for a three-year term and until a successor is elected and qualified in accordance with the Beverly Home Rule Charter

**FLSA Status:** Non-Exempt

**Union:** No

### Position Summary

The Budget/Management Analyst performs a legislative oversight and a post-audit function and is not involved in the day-to-day administrative detail of the financial operations of the city. The budget/management analyst shall have free access to all books, accounts, bills and vouchers of the city and shall continuously review and examine the same. The budget/management analyst shall make periodic reports thereon to the city council, with such frequency as the city council by ordinance, by rule or by other vote may direct, but not less frequently than quarterly. All officials of the city shall cooperate with the budget/management analyst in the performance of this oversight function. The budget/management analyst may have other powers and duties as may be provided by the City Charter of the City of Beverly, or by ordinance or by other vote of the City Council. The position supports the City Council in carrying out its legislative responsibilities while remaining independent of the City's day-to-day financial administration.

The Analyst provides objective financial analysis and recommendations regarding the annual operating budget, capital improvement program, appropriations, financial forecasts, internal controls, and other fiscal matters.

### Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Include the following; other duties may be assigned.

#### Budget and Financial Analysis

- From time to time throughout the year examine, or cause to be examined, the books and accounts of all City agencies which are entrusted with the receipt, custody or expenditure of money, including original bills on which money has been paid from the City treasury, the documentation submitted by the agency requesting payment of any such bills supporting such payment, the warrants for the payments of bills and the canceled checks on file in the office of the City Treasurer.
- At least once in every year verify, or cause to be verified, the cash balance of each such City agency by the actual count of the cash on hand and by reconciliation of bank balances.

#### Reporting and Advisory Services

- Keep the City Council President fully informed as to the results of this activity and, not less frequently than quarterly, shall make a detailed report summarizing the results of this overview to the City Council Standing Committee on Finance and Property.
- All reports to the full City Council shall be made through the City Council Standing Committee on Finance and Property.
- Review each request which is made to the City Council by the Mayor, as provided in Beverly Home Rule Charter Section 6-7, for the transfer of funds or for a supplementary appropriation, and shall make a report to the City Council Standing Committee on Finance and Property, including a recommendation as to the action to be taken by the City Council, before the City Council acts on the matter.
- When the proposed capital improvement program is submitted to the City Council ~~by the Mayor, as required by Beverly Home Rule Charter Section 6-8, the~~ Budget/Management Analyst shall review the proposed capital improvement program and shall, before the same is submitted to the City Council for any action, make a report, including specific recommendations for actions to be taken by the City Council concerning the capital improvement program as seem necessary, desirable or expedient.
- When the proposed annual operating budget is submitted to the City Council by the Mayor, as provided in Beverly Home Rule Charter Section 6-3, the Budget/Management Analyst shall review the proposed annual operating budget and shall, before the proposed operating budget is submitted to the City Council for any action, make a report, including recommendations of specific actions to be taken by the City Council concerning the annual operating budget and any part or parts thereof as seem necessary, desirable or expedient.

#### Records Access and Other Duties

- Shall have the power and authority to call upon any agency of the City government to submit for inspection by them the agency's books and vouchers, and to furnish any information pertaining to the financial conduct of the departments.
- Shall be appointed as an ex-officio member of the Financial Forecasting Committee.
- May have other powers and duties as may be provided by the City Charter of the City of Beverly, or by ordinance or by other vote of the City Council.
- Work cooperatively with City departments, especially the finance department, while maintaining independence and objectivity.
- Maintain confidentiality of sensitive information.

### Minimum Qualifications:

#### Education and Experience

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Public Administration, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
- Three to five years of progressively responsible experience in governmental finance, budgeting, accounting, auditing, or municipal administration.
- Municipal government experience preferred.
- Equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.

### Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

#### Knowledge of

- Governmental accounting (GAAP/GASB), municipal budgeting, auditing, and internal controls.
- Public finance, capital planning, debt management, and Massachusetts municipal finance laws.
- Financial reporting, public administration, and municipal financial systems (MUNIS or similar).
- Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word.

#### Ability to

- Analyze complex financial data and develop sound recommendations.
- Interpret financial statements, budgets, and applicable laws.
- Prepare clear written reports and present information effectively.
- Manage multiple priorities, exercise independent judgment, and maintain confidentiality.
- Build effective working relationships with elected officials, employees, auditors, and the public.
- Strong Oral and Communications Skills

#### Work Environment and Schedule

- This is a part-time position with variable hours based on operational needs.
- Approximately 75% of the work may be performed remotely, with the remaining time spent at City Hall or other City locations as required.
- Attendance at evening City Council meetings and other meetings is expected.
- Work is performed primarily in an office environment and requires prolonged periods of sitting, frequent computer use, and occasional lifting of up to 10 pounds.
